findings.failure_scenario: Dead code clutters the script and adds unnecessary maintenance overhead.
findings.summary: The DIM color variable is defined but never used in the installer script.

findings.failure_scenario: The script includes an unused function, increasing size and maintenance surface without adding value.
findings.summary: The info() function is defined but never called in the installer script.

findings.failure_scenario: Maintainers may unknowingly modify or rely on this untested dead helper, adding complexity to the test suite.
findings.summary: The t() helper function is defined but never called in the test script.

findings.failure_scenario: If the downloaded binary is incompatible with the host system (e.g. glibc mismatch or missing dynamic libraries), it will crash when run. The installer catches this with `|| warn ...` but fails to exit 1, incorrectly reporting a successful installation to the user.
findings.summary: The post-install verification step emits a warning when the installed binary fails to run, but still allows the script to exit 0.

findings.failure_scenario: If the checksum validation logic in the script is fundamentally broken, removed, or accidentally changed to log a warning instead of failing, the test suite will still pass, providing false confidence.
findings.summary: The checksum mismatch test is vacuous because it only greps the script source code for the error message instead of exercising the failure path.

command: awk '/Network-dependent rows/,0 { if (/^(    t_grep|    n=\$\(\(n \+ 1\)\))/) print $0}' scripts/tests/install_test.sh | wc -l
findings.failure_scenario: When the network check fails, the script outputs 'skipping the 6 network-dependent rows below', misleading developers into thinking only 6 tests were skipped when 9 tests actually were.
findings.summary: The hardcoded count of network-dependent rows skipped is 6, but there are actually 9 tests executed in the network block.

findings.failure_scenario: If a command that consumes stdin is added to the script, it will swallow the rest of the script when run via `curl | sh`, causing a critical silent failure. Running `sh script.sh` instead of piping to `sh` fails to catch this execution behavior divergence.
findings.summary: The test suite executes the installer using `sh scripts/install.sh`, completely missing the pipe execution mode (`curl ... | sh`) it intends to simulate.

json_schema.title: PR-REVIEW-SKILL-002 v2 §3.E — the structured output agy is asked for
json_schema.$comment: NOT under schemas/. That directory is VENDORED UPSTREAM artifacts only — two files, a SHA-256 manifest and a sources.json recording where each came from, enforced by scripts/check_vendored_schemas.sh and its own mutation guard. This schema is authored here, has no upstream, and would have no honest row in sources.json; putting it there would make a provenance record that records nothing. It is the skill's own output contract, so it lives with the skill.

reviewed.description: false means agy declined or could not review. The caller records status: unreachable and verdict DEGRADED — never a run that found nothing.

findings.description: May be empty. An empty array under reviewed:true is 'ran and found nothing', which is a different artifact from 'could not run' (§3.0).

grounding.description: §1's three marks and there is no fourth. A `measured` finding here was measured by AGY's process, not the primary reviewer's — the receipt records that in reverified_by_primary (§3.E.5).

failure_scenario.description: §4.2: a finding that cannot name the concrete failure it permits is a comment, not a finding.

source.description: Required by the guard when grounding is `cited`: a citation with no source is an assertion wearing the mark of a citation (§1.1).

command.description: argv, when grounding is `measured`. It records what AGY ran, and the primary reviewer does not re-run it (§3.E.5).
